body.p: Applicant has amended independent claims 1, 17, and 20 and dependent claims 4, 7, 9-12, and 16. Claims 3, 5, and 6 have been cancelled without prejudice or any disclaimer. New claims 21-23 have been added. No new matter has been introduced.
Claims 1, 2, 4, and 7-23 are currently pending in the application, with claims 1, 17, and 20 being in independent form.
Based on the above amendments and the following remarks, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner reconsider this application and withdraw all outstanding rejections.

Claims 6-10 and 14-15 are objected to as being dependent upon a rejected base claim, but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims. See Office Action, p. 6.

Applicant thanks the Examiner for indicating that claims 6-10 and 14-15 include allowable subject matter. As shown in the claim amendment section, the subject matter of claim 6 indicated by the Examiner as allowable, as well as the subject matter of claims 3 and 5 from which claim 6 depends, has been incorporated into independent claims 1, 17, and 20, placing these independent claims, and thus the present application, in condition for allowance.
Claims 1-5, 11-13, and 16-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Kuwahara (US 2014/0236565). See Office Action, p. 2.
Without acquiescing to the propriety of the rejection and to expedite the prosecution,

Applicant has amended independent claim 1 to incorporate the allowable subject matter of claim 6, as well as the subject matter of claims 3 and 5 from which claim 6 depends, to place claim 1 in condition for allowance. Dependent claims 2, 4, and 7-16 are also in condition for allowance due to their dependence from base claim 1.

Independent claims 17 and 20, while of different scope, include recitations similar to those of claim 1. Thus, claims 17 and 20, as well as claims 18-19 and 21-23 respectively dependent therefrom, are also in condition for allowance.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests that the 35 U.S.C. § 102 rejection be withdrawn.

All of the stated grounds of rejections have been properly traversed, accommodated, or rendered moot. Applicant therefore respectfully requests that the Examiner reconsider the application and timely allow the pending claims. If the Examiner believes, for any reason, that personal communication will expedite prosecution of this application, the Examiner is invited to telephone the undersigned at the number provided.
Prompt and favorable consideration of this Reply is respectfully requested.
